test_title: SSC CGL 2022 Tier-I Official Paper (Held On : 07 Dec 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Who wrote the book titled 'Gift to Monotheism'?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Raja Ram Mohan Roy**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **"Gift to Monotheists"** was written by** Raja Ram Mohan Roy in 1809** and translated into **Bengali**.
 
• **Raja Ram Mohan Roy** was an outstanding social reformer in India who supported monotheism and provided evidence for it in the old **Hindu texts.**
 
• Often referred to as the** founder of modern India** and the** father of the Indian Renaissance, Raja Ram Mohan Roy** lived from 1772 to 1833.
 
• He was given the** title "Raja" by Akbar II.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Swami Vivekanand**

 
 
• ​**Swami Vivekananda**, whose real name was **Narendranath Datta**, was an Indian Hindu monk, philosopher, writer, and religious teacher. He was also **Ramakrishna's** most important pupil.
 
• He lived from 12 January 1863 to 4 July 1902. He is credited with promoting interfaith understanding and elevating **Hinduism** to the position of a significant international religion. He was a vital player in the introduction of **Vedanta** and **Yoga** to the **Western** **world**.
 
 
 
• **Dayanand Saraswati**
 
 
• **​Dayananda** **Saraswati**, an **Indian** philosopher and social reformer who founded the **Arya** **Samaj**, a Vedic dharma reform movement, lived from 12 February 1824 to 30 October 1883.
 
• In 1876, he was the first to make the plea for Swaraj as "**India for Indians**," which **Lokmanya** Tilak eventually embraced.
 
 
 
• **Kehsavchand Sen**
 
 
• **​Keshub** **Chandra** **Sen**, a Hindu philosopher and social reformer who lived from 19 November 1838 to 8 January 1884, made an effort to integrate **Christian theology** with **Hinduism**.
 
• He was a Hindu who was born in the** Bengal Presidency of British India **and joined the **Brahmo Samaj** in 1857 before starting his own breakaway group, the "**Bharatvarshiya Brahmo Samaj**," in 1866 while the **Brahmo Samaj** was still run by **Debendranath Tagore.**
 
 

a9:T
